extracted.intended_audience: readers and reporters focused on platform governance, tech policy, and democracy implications of major tech companies
extracted.subtask_description: Selecting and curating ‘must-read’ stories about platforms where technology, governance, and democracy intersect; guidance for prioritizing items for a front-page newsletter. Emphasizes civic impact, precedent, power dynamics, and internal revelations over product fluff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust & safety implications
rubrics_metrics.description: does this affect how billions experience platforms?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize stories that change user safety, exposure to harm, or the mechanisms platforms use to moderate or surface content; focus on scale and real-world effects rather than technical details with no user-facing change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power shift
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight stories that alter the balance of power between platforms, users, governments, or other institutions — e.g., changes to moderation authority, ownership, regulatory reach, or corporate governance that reallocate control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedent setting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elevate novel decisions or policies that create a template others may follow (platform or regulator); emphasize potential for repeatability and long-term industry impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal dissent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value internal documents, memos, or reporting that show employees or contractors questioning a platform’s direction or policies — indicative of internal conflict and cues to systemic issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content moderation tensions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on stories exposing trade-offs platforms make between protecting expression, preventing harm, and monetization pressures; signal where incentives create conflicts with public-interest outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-and-society
rubrics_metrics.description: model behavior with downstream user impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize research, incidents, or policy developments that show how models affect people’s experiences, decisions, or civic processes — not abstract model benchmarks but societal effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: "What did everyone in tech wake up thinking about?"
rubrics_metrics.description: "What did everyone in tech wake up thinking about?" (Newton's stated selection prompt)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a salience test: stories that dominate the tech conversation that morning or signal an immediate shift in industry attention deserve front-page treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Which decision today will be cited in five years?"
rubrics_metrics.description: "Which decision today will be cited in five years?" (Newton's stated selection prompt)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess longevity and lasting significance: prefer developments likely to be referenced in future accounts of platform-era policy or practice rather than ephemeral news.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Where did the consensus shift?"
rubrics_metrics.description: "Where did the consensus shift?" (Newton's stated selection prompt)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for inflection points where industry, regulators, or public opinion move — stories that mark a change in thinking, norms, or accepted practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Where did a platform act like a state?"
rubrics_metrics.description: "Where did a platform act like a state?" (Newton's stated selection prompt)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spot actions by platforms that resemble governmental power (setting rules for millions, enforcing norms, adjudicating disputes) and examine implications for governance and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: product launches without behavior change
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deprioritize product announcements that do not meaningfully alter user behavior, business model, or policy — avoid treating routine feature updates as front-page news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: incremental quarterly earnings (unless thesis-breaking)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skip routine financial reports unless they contradict prevailing narratives or materially change the outlook for a platform’s strategy or power; only elevate earnings that break an important thesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: personality drama without policy stakes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid coverage focused on individuals’ antics or celebrity disputes unless those stories reveal policy, governance, or structural implications for platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: tech-press groupthink takes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist amplifying repetitive, uncritical industry narratives; seek original reporting or analysis rather than reiteration of common talking points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: researcher findings on platform harm
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize credible academic or independent research that documents harms, mechanisms, or causal links — especially studies with implications for policy or platform practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: internal documents (Facebook Papers style)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give prominence to leaked or released internal materials that reveal intent, trade-offs, or knowledge within platforms; these often expose discrepancies between public claims and internal practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: whistleblower disclosures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat firsthand disclosures by insiders as high-priority when they credibly illuminate wrongdoing, negligence, or systemic problems with broad public consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: court rulings reshaping platform liability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight legal rulings that change the liability landscape for platforms or set new standards for how platforms are regulated or sued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: new regulatory frameworks (EU DSA, UK OSB)
rubrics_metrics.description: New regulatory frameworks (EU DSA, UK OSB)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on implementation or interpretation of major regulatory regimes that will govern platform behavior across jurisdictions; cover consequential rulemaking and enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: election-integrity related platform decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize actions by platforms that could affect electoral processes, misinformation flows around elections, or access to civic information — due to high civic-stakes impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overarching principle: civic/democratic intersection
rubrics_metrics.description: Tech news is most newsworthy when it intersects with democratic, civic, or rights-bearing infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use civic impact as a guiding lens: prefer stories showing how platform decisions touch rights, governance, public institutions, or democratic processes rather than purely commercial or technical developments.
